messages:
Jordan (support): FYI customer acct-acme hit a big embedding invoice this morning — invoice INV-2026-00345 shows ~24.8k embedding units billed but the dashboard for the project shows ~9.4k embeddings. Can someone triage? :confused:
Priya (billing): Got the invoice id, pulling metering logs now. Did they run any rerank or pairwise flows? Those can blow up numbers if counted differently.
Jordan (support): Customer says they only call embeddings + a separate rerank endpoint for candidate scoring, but they expect rerank to be counted as CPU/rerank, not double-charged as embeddings.
Priya (billing): Looking at raw metering events for acct-acme between 2026-03-15T00:00 and 2026-03-15T23:59 — I see two streams: embedding.create events ~9,412 and rerank.score_pairwise events ~15,400. The invoice line item lumps both as "embedding units" for this billing period because a backend classification rule tagged pairwise scoring as embedding-like consumption.
Ethan (eng-ml): That classification is intentional for some variants historically (we bill per vector produced). But there was a recent internal change in how rerank requests are expanded in batching: when a batch contains queries with candidate lists we expand to pairwise tasks and emit both embedding.create and rerank.pair metrics. That double emits both metrics for the same vector in certain code paths. Looks like acct-acme hit that code path.
Maya (sre): Is there a repro we can run quickly? I can emulate with a small candidate set to see what events are emitted.
Jordan (support): Customer provided sample payload — they sent a batched rerank request with 1 query + 10 candidates. They also call embeddings separately for indexing. I'll paste sanitized example below.
Jordan (support): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{
   "model": "rerank-lite-1",
   "query": "How to optimize inference costs?",
   "candidates": ["candidate A text...","candidate B text...", "candidate C text..." /* 10 total */],
   "batch_id": "batch-20260315-1"
 }'
```
Ethan (eng-ml): When the runtime expands it produces N candidate embeddings and then runs pairwise scoring. Metering should either: (a) count embeddings only when returned to the customer, or (b) count rerank pairwise operations as a separate metric and not duplicate the embedding count. Right now some paths do both.
Priya (billing): I also see several 5xx retries around 2026-03-15T08:12:02 for the same batch_id. The client retried without idempotency-key -> duplicates were billed as new events. Example from logs: 
```
2026-03-15T08:12:01Z INFO request id=req-abc-1 batch_id=batch-20260315-1 status=500
2026-03-15T08:12:05Z INFO request id=req-abc-2 batch_id=batch-20260315-1 status=200
```
Jordan (support): Customer dev says their client didn't set Idempotency-Key by accident. So some of the extra counts are probably due to retries. But that still doesn't explain why rerank shows up as embedding units on the invoice.
Ethan (eng-ml): Agreed — two separate issues: (1) duplication from retries, and (2) a classification/aggregation bug that folds rerank pairwise consumption into embeddings line items. I'll open a PR to stop emitting duplicate embedding.create events during rerank expansion and to add a safeguard to de-duplicate by request id + batch_id when possible.
Maya (sre): For immediate repro I ran a small test: one query + 3 candidates batched -> metering events (order): embedding.create x3, rerank.score_pairwise x3, then embedding.create x3 emitted AGAIN on the expansion path. So yes, duplication exists.
Priya (billing): Ok. Action plan: 1) create billing ops ticket to hold invoice INV-2026-00345 pending investigation and potential credit, 2) engineering to patch duplicate emission + correction script to recompute affected customers for 2026-03-01..2026-03-15, 3) communicate to customer the temporary cause (retries + rerank aggregation) and ETA for credit.
Ethan (eng-ml): WIP PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank-metering/pull/412 — main changes: dedupe by (request_id|idempotency_key) and make rerank produce only rerank.pair metrics (no embedding.create) unless the embedding vector is returned in the API response payload.
Jordan (support): For the short-term ask: can billing ops provide a draft note we can send to the customer explaining "why" and the expected credit?
Priya (billing): Draft ready, will send via ticket with explanation + estimate. Also need to ask accounting about issuing a partial credit — I'll CC accounting.
Maya (sre): Quick mitigation for clients: recommend setting an Idempotency-Key header and limiting batch sizes for rerank (e.g., max 16 candidates) until patch is deployed. I'll add a blurb to the status page.
Jordan (support): Customer asked: will vector dims mismatch affect billing? They noticed different embedding dims between index runs and rerank responses.
Ethan (eng-ml): That can happen if different models/variants are used. We bill per vector unit; larger dims effectively cost more if we normalize by dimensionality in our billing unit. Confirmed the customer used "embed-small-512" for indexing and rerank used "rerank-large-768" internally for scoring; our metering translates those into different unit multipliers. We'll include that in the explanation.
Priya (billing): Summarizing root causes: (A) duplicate emission on rerank expansion, (B) client retries without idempotency, (C) aggregation rule that mapped rerank pairwise into embedding line item. We'll reconcile invoices where customers were materially affected.
Jordan (support): Thanks all. I'll update the customer thread with a short explanation and the mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-00345 status: ON_HOLD (billing_ops/12345). Reason: metering investigation.
Priya (billing): I'll follow up in billing_ops ticket 12345 with proposed credit amount and timeline. Expect update by EOD PST.
Ethan (eng-ml): Follow-up items for eng: PR to dedupe (in review), migration/repair job to recompute affected line items, add unit tests for batch expansion, and telemetry dashboard to surface rerank vs embedding counts separately.
Maya (sre): I'll post a short status update to #status and add mitigation guidance to the docs page on metering best practices.
Jordan (support): Closing loop with customer now. If anyone needs the raw sanitized logs or customer payloads for the billing ops ticket let me know.
